sentences.text: It is the case of the claimant that on 27.08.2005 at about 3.30 p.m., the claimant along with other passengers, were travelling in a bus from Belvai towards Hukratte side when the bus reached near Sanoor High School the driver of the said Bus drove the vehicle in a sharp curve in a rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle.

As a result the bus fell on the NC:
2023:KHC:37653 right side of the road and many passengers in the bus were injured.

3. According to the claimant he is an agriculturist and earning an amount of Rs.8,000/- per month and because of the injuries sustained in the accident as per Exhibit-P26, wound certificate he has sustained fracture of distal radius left and apart from this grievous injury the claimant also sustained other simple injuries and he was treated as inpatient from 27.08.2005 to 07.09.2005 in Father Muller Hospital Mangalore.

He had also filed the medical bills amounting to Rs.15,15,046/-
and no Doctor was examined and nothing was placed on record to show that he had sustained permanent partial disability.
Taking into consideration the injuries the court below had awarded an amount of Rs.40,000/- as global compensation.

4. Learned counsel appearing for the claimant submits that the claimant had sustained a fracture injury NC: 2023:KHC:37653 and the court below without granting the compensation on various heads had granted a global compensation of an amount of Rs.40,000/- which is not appropriate.
Claimant had sustained injuries and had undergone pain and suffering and for the transportation and for the laid up period he is entitled for the compensation.
5.

Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that as the treated Doctor was not examined and except the Wound Certificate no other material was placed before the court below, the court below had granted a global compensation of Rs.40,000/-.
6. Having heard the learned counsel on either side perused the entire material on record.

In this case as per Exhibit-P26, wound certificate the claimant had sustained a fracture injury and hence under the head of pain and suffering the claimant is entitled for a sum of Rs.30,000/- and towards Francis Vaz vs P M Narayana on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74786198/
2

sentences.text: Medical Expenses he had produced bills amounting to Rs.15,046/-.

It is stated that NC:
2023:KHC:37653 the claimant was earning Rs.8,000/- per month.

As this is an accident of the year 2008, this Court is inclined to consider the monthly income at Rs.4,000/- per month, this Court is inclined to grant an amount of Rs.12,000/-, towards transportation, attendant and nourishment an amount of Rs.5,000/- is awarded.

7. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA vs. M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards Legal Expenses.

sentences.text:
8. The claimant is therefore, entitled to the compensation under the following heads:
(2014) 11 SCC 178 NC: 2023:KHC:37653 Heads Compensation Awarded 1. Pain and Sufferings : Rs. 30,000/-
2. Loss of Earning during laid up period : Rs. 12,000/-
(Rs.4,000 x 3 )
3.

Medical Expenses : Rs. 10,000/-
4. Transportation, Attendant and : Rs. 5,000/-
Nourishment 5.

Legal Expenses : Rs. 10,000/-
TOTAL : Rs. 67,000/-
9.

Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed, enhancing the compensation amount from Rs.40,000/-
to Rs.67,000/-.
(i) The enhanced amount shall carry interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
ii) The respondent - insurance company shall deposit the amount within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of copy of the judgment.

On NC:
2023:KHC:37653 such deposit, the claimant is entitled to withdraw the entire amount without furnishing any security.
iii) Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
Francis Vaz vs P M Narayana on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74786198/
3 iv) No costs.
